To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed a new tool, VarCount, that allows for the quantification and analysis of variants in a sample at the individual level and we found enrichment for compound heterozoys in genes involved in neurodevelopment in a cohort of epileptic encephelopathy patients.

1) We present VarCount, a tool for variant quantification at the individual level, 2) We used VarCount on Epi4k patients and 1000 genomes project participants to detect enrichment of recessive compound heterozygotes, and 3) We identified enrichment in three genes, PRTG (Neuronal Growth and Development), MACF1 (Neuronal Development) and TNC (Neuronal Migration) in the patients with epilepsy.
we have developed a tool for quantifying variants and applied it to the Epi4K data to detect enrichment for compound heterozgous variants in three genes involved in neuronal growth.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the genetic variation in human populations and the impact of this variation in human health and disease.
the identification of compound heterozygotes in the Epi4K data set.
the identification of genes that are involved in the pathogenesis of epilepsy and the development of novel therapeutic approaches.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we did not detect any statistically significant enrichment of compound heterozygotes in genes involved in neurodevelopmental processes in the Epi4K data.
the results are not statistically significant, but that the findings are interesting and worth following up.

our results suggest that the genes TNC, MACF1, PRTG and possibly others may be novel candidates for recessive epileptic encephalo-pathies, however, the statistical significance is low, and the data needs to be replicated in larger studies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
compound heterozygoty is a feature of recessive epilepsy genes.
compound heterozygosities are enriched in genes involved in growth and development of the central nervous system.
compound heterozyous variants are enriched in genes involved in neural development and growth, but that further validation is needed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
VarCount is a useful tool for the quantification, characterization and comparison of variants in different populations and can be applied to any dataset containing variants identified by sequencing.
the use of VarCount can help researchers to identify compound heterozygote variants in a given population.

VarCount is a powerful tool to assess compound heterozygosity at the individual level and that the enrichment for recessive variants in the Epi4K dataset is a promising finding that warrants further investigation.
